en:
Subspace warp drive
disengaged. We are now in
orbit around our
destination.

Oho, and I have confirmed
the existence of at least
one metropolis! This
planet's population is, in all
likelihood, a rather
advanced one.
Splendid. If that's the\ncase, mayhap we can at\nlast find some parts.
That surely would make\nour task exceedingly easy.

In the process, maybe I
could procure a little
something to enhance my
specifications.

At any rate, as I spy some
waterways a distance
from our potential landing
site, I hereby dub this
celestial body <font color=yellow>Farbrooke</font>.

Understood and already
planned for, Captain. It
should be far enough from
any residential areas that
no one witnesses us touch
down.

As long as this place is
more peaceful than the
last few, I have no qualms
with being seen.
What seems to be the\nmatter? Did we\ncrash-land!?

That is the most spurious
libel I have ever heard! ...I
am innocent, I tell you! I
was framed! I demand a
lawyer! I have yet to even
be read my rights!

Ladies and gentlemen of
the court, the truth is...our
humble vessel is under
attack as we speak!
How is that even\npossible!? Who could be\nattacking us?

Some defense system
specifically designed to
eradicate invaders, a local
population angry at our
unannounced visit, or even
some bloodthirsty native
fauna!

No matter how thick the
hull is, a concentrated
attack could easily
rupture it, potentially even
resulting in an explosion!

That would blow us to
kingdom come! Forget
sleeping with the fishes;
we would be orbiting with
the electrons, so
microscopic would our
remains be!
Oh dear, oh dear! My\nsincerest apologies. Ah,\nyes!
A capital idea! I\nwholeheartedly support\nyou fighting fire with fire!
The safety of this ship is\nin your hands, Captain. Do\nus proud.
I knew I could count on\nyou! Now the ship can live\nto fly another day.
Who were those\nreprobates, anyway?

From the transmissions I
intercepted, it appears
they are a rebel group at
war with the current
administration.
What reason could rebels\nhave for attacking\noutsiders such as us?
Have a listen and you just\nmay find out.

Whodda thunk some
ship'd land right in front of
us? That lucky bunny's
foot musta paid off.
Let's loot it and split\nwhat we get between the\nlot of us.

I'm with ya on that. Not
like this was part of the
mission, so we don't hafta
tell the bosses nothin'.

Yeah. Plus, not like one
little ship's gonna have the
same type of goods a
city's got. Damn, can't wait
to get mah hands on some
more booty, if ya catch
mah drift.
Hahaha! Don't we all?\nHell, the next raid can't\ncome soon enough.
How dare they call\nthemselves "rebels"!?

They endeavor not to
overthrow oppressive
governments, but to
plunder helpless citizens!

To think of all the homes
they have razed, the
families they have torn
apart... It sickens me.

We cannot stand idly by
while these brigands
destroy a planet's
civilization! We must face
them!
Let's make things right.
Yes. They threaten our\nmission.
We might even be\nrewarded for our efforts!

That's what I like to see
from you! Now let us give
them a taste of their own
medicine!
I knew it would come to\nthis... I felt it in my gears.\nFelt it in my gears, I did.

Please at least try to
respect the UP3 and keep
your involvement to a
minimum.

I agree. Judging from their
nefarious deeds, it is only
a matter of time before
we clash with them again.
It might as well be now.
A grand idea! Go from\nrags to riches in one\nmission!

They seem to have a large
following―and we know
how ruthless they are―so
their eradication would
have to fetch a hefty
price!

Exactly! And once their TV
networks know of our tale,
we shall have fame as
well!

Oh, how we shall live! I will
drink of their finest
machine oils from goblets
of their purest crystal in
mansions of their poshest
design!

Was this not supposed to
be a stopover on the way
back to Earth? Have you
the attention spans of
gerels?
*Sigh* I'll take what I can\nget. At least you want to\ncooperate.
All right, it is time to shift\nfocus!

From here on out, we
concentrate on finding
those bandits! Over and
out!

Shower me with praise,
Captain, for none in the
galaxy is more deserving
of it!

How can one tiny machine
be possessed of such
amazing faculties!? In the
face of insurmountable
odds, stranded in a
faraway star system, this
robot has done it!

Would you mind singing
your own praises at a
lower volume―preferably
zero?

I would if I could, but I
have discovered a new
rebel base under
construction!
You have!? Are you for\ncertain!?
Beyond a shadow of a\ndoubt!

Wonderful! Though I am
loath to admit it, that
deserves at least a pat on
the head.
At last! How I have waited\nfor this day!
...Ew! Disgusting!
Remove those unseemly\nappendages from my\nsight.

I-I apologize. I promise
that, one day, my dainty
legs shall be as muscular
as my macho guns.

To be honest, I would
rather not see either your
legs or your so-called
"guns" again.
Can we please return to\nthe matter at hand?
Not only regarding the\nrebels, but regarding the\nplanet itself.

More important than intel
though, we may also find
parts for our ship at the
base. After all, it is still
under construction.
As such, the majority of\ntheir leadership will likely\nbe stationed elsewhere.
Alas, could we but dispose\nof them all with one fell\nblow...

Just because their
leadership is absent does
not mean they will be
weak. Stay alert.
A salient point. Perhaps\nwe can use the shadows\nas our allies?

Were we to sneak in and
disrupt their logistics, that
would be hindrance
enough.
Then it is decided! We\nprioritize stealth over the\nuse of force.

You have my thanks for
clearing us a path and
allowing us to infiltrate the
base, but I have some
questions.
How do you explain this?

Is this not one of the
towers that emits jamming
signals? And why does its
interior resemble a mine?
I scanned the building,\nand it is indeed one of\nthose towers.

Perhaps...these 'rebels'
are part of that illegal
mining operation, and it
spans multiple star
systems? It sounds
ridiculous, but―
I hear someone! Hide!
The hell's with this place\nanyway? It's ginormous!
For the love of...I thought I\nexplained this to ya.

The tower emits
electromagnetic waves.
Those waves change the
rock below into a precious
metal.

Our client needs this
metal as an energy
source, so they pay us to
mine it. If you're ever
gonna be our business
ambassador―
Ha, you said "ass"!

*Sigh* ...You're such an
idiot. Lemme put it in
terms you'll understand.
Tower equals money.

But how's we gonna make
money when the tower
keeps breakin' our
transmitters and stuff?
Transmitters not workin' is\na good thing.

If our electronics don't
work, the government's
don't either. They can't
keep tabs on us!
Now cram it. We gotta\ncapture those intruders,\nremember?
They should be gone now.
Well, we came here looking\nfor leads, and we found\nsome.

We certainly did. The
federation possesses
similar technology to what
the rebels described.

They must have figured
out how to adapt it for
large-scale mining
operations.

Therefore, once this
tower is completed, the
ship's sensors are going
to be in trouble again.
I never expected the\njamming to be a mere side\neffect.

Let us not forget the
sudden changes to
Esperance's ecosystem. It
is safe to assume those
were related as well.

So they care not a whit
for these planets as long
as they can extract their
precious metals!?

My blood boils simply
thinking about this! Coro,
is there no way you can
prevent the tower from
emitting energy?

I can negate it in a
localized area for a short
period of time, like how a
counter-jammer works.

To nullify it completely,
however, would require a
much more detailed
analysis of the energy.
How naive of me to think\nanything would come easy\non this mission.
That does make sense. At\nleast we were able to\nascertain their objective.

I hardly agree with their
actions, but I understand
the allure of money often
trumps one's cares for
their environment.

I cannot fathom, however,
why their client requires
extensive amounts of
precious metals.

Fortunately for us, some
representative of this
"client" must be here,
otherwise how would the
rebels know how to
construct this tower?

Now that we have their
scent, all that's left is to
hunt this puppetmaster
down!
Following the trail of\nrebels should lead us\nstraight to our quarry!

Amongst the documents
we recovered from the
tower are plans detailing a
raid of the nearby city.

Oh, we certainly do, as
they were kind enough to
include their rendezvous
point.
Now that we have this\nintel, we're obviously going\nto intercept them...right?
Why wouldn't we?
Yes, as I want to know\nwho this client is.
Yup! I wanna make the\nlocals swoon for me.
I knew we would be on the\nsame page.

You should look before
you leap. This is a raiding
party, so it will consist of
their most savage
warriors.

How I despise your
incessant calculating.
Have you never heard the
phrase "man up"? You
would do well to heed it.

I...hate to burst your
bubble, but I am an
artificial intelligence.
Concepts like gender roles
do not apply to me.

Indeed! As their leaders
will be present, some of
them should know
something!

Perhaps they might even
possess information about
who is behind the mining
operation!

You would put your life on
the line for the same
reason high school
students pick up the
guitar?

No use denying that
humans view dedication as
sexy, E.V.E.! And Captain
is as dedicated as they
come!

Either way, we are to
ambush the rebels at their
rendezvous point,
correct?
Aye. Let us make for it so\nwe can flesh out the rest\nof our plan!

Oh, that reminds me; the
raid's zero hour is in
exactly forty-seven
minutes.
Why did you wait until now\nto say that!?
Congratulations on\nsuccessfully defending the\ncity, Captain!
Ohoho! And just what\nintelligence might that be?
The leader was in\npossession of a map.

It delineates three points
of operation and routes
that connect them to
each other.
The first is where the raid\nwas to transpire.
The second is the tower\nwe surreptitiously entered.
The third is a base\nroughly equidistant from\nthe first two.

These two roads have the
look of supply routes to
me, meaning the third
point is quite possibly
their headquarters.
Aye aye! I shall do all in\nmy power to investigate\nthat location!

My analysis of the area
surrounding the location
on that rebel map is
progressing nicely.

I do hope it is their
headquarters. That would
save us an immense
amount of time.

On the other hand, it
being their headquarters
would make it all the more
dangerous and difficult to
infiltrate.

Ah, fretful little Coro. I
remember being told this
proverb when I once
expressed worries such as
yours. Mayhap it will
embolden you as it did me.
You cannot pluck a\ngolden apple without\nfacing Ladon.
...Who is Ladon?
Huh? Oh, well, he...

He is a dragon of legend.
He had one hundred
heads and stood watch
over apples that granted
immortality.

That seems a bit farcical,
no? His body would have
to be massive to support
a hundred heads. You
could probably
outmaneuver him easily.

Besides, dragons are
animals and need sleep
too. You could just wait
until he went to bed and
steal some apples then.

Furthermore, what if he
watches over a whole
orchard? I find it hard to
believe he could protect
all those trees at once.
That's a straw man! And a\ntextbook example, if I dare\nsay so!

What? But I am
addressing your argument.
I am giving viable
alternatives―
All I wanted to say was\nthat reward almost never\ncomes without risk!

I-I see. I guess I was a bit
too concerned with the
details and failed to look
at the big picture.

Well, if we are to risk so
much with this attack,
then we had best be
prepared!

(Wait. Does her
recollection of a proverb
mean her memory has
returned?)
The rebels have raised\nthe white flag! Rejoice!\nVictory is ours!
Oh! Oh! Apparently our\njob is not yet done. Enemy\nretreating at ten o'clock!
What!? I thought we\ndispatched―

Hmmm...he looks a tad too
regal to be the rebels'
leader... Could that
mean...!?

You may be mere pests,
but you have more brains
than government lapdogs.
They could never get this
far.

I assume then you are the
maggots from the tower
incident? How satisfying it
will be to squash you.
You shan't escape!\n...Captain, we must pursue\nhim!
No need to be so hard on\nyourself, E.V.E.
How can I not? He was\nwithin arm's reach!

Honestly, I am surprised
you even got that close.
Who knew your speed was
practically superhuman?

Your praise is no
substitute for his capture,
Coro. I will turn over every
stone on this planet if it
means apprehending that
degenerate!
You can leave those\nstones unturned, as I can\ntrace his current location.
What? You can?
Why would I not be able\nto? The ship's sensors\nwork on this planet.

And when, pray tell, were
you thinking of divulging
such important
information to us? Never?

Correct. Seeing how
motivated you were, I did
not want to "take the wind
out of your sails."

No, please! O, omnipotent
Evelysse! Take pity on this
humble bucket of bolts
and spare his life!

Though I may not be
deserving of your infinite
largess, I sincerely hope
you find it within yourself
to... Noooooo! I am too
young to diiie!
That's one nuisance down,\nso let us now quell the\nother!
The remaining rebel forces\nshould be holed up in this\nstructure.
Do you happen to know\nthe structure's purpose?

I must say, that thought
had never crossed my
mind! It does seem like
perfect housing for a
spacecraft.

You never cease to
amaze, Captain! I would
venture they likely have
some materials for tower
construction in there too!
We shall never have a\nbetter opportunity than\nthis.
What makes you say\nthat?

Though we may not
possess much intelligence
on them, they cannot
possibly have any on us.

Is it in their best interest
to invest all their
resources into
exterminating us? Would it
be more prudent to simply
cut their losses and flee?

They do not know, and
this indecision will
hopefully cloud their
judgment.
At this moment, they are\nas vulnerable as we can\never expect them to be.

Good thinking! War is
waged not only on
physical fronts, but
psychological ones as well.

If only I could more
accurately predict how
humans will respond under
duress. Sadly, it is beyond
my capabilities.

Even though you are so
human yourself? Never
have I seen an AI with
such an expressive
countenance...disturbing
as it may be.

Thank you so much for
the kind words! ...Except I
think you meant to say
"dignified" or
"distinguished," not
"disturbing"!

You clearly do not have a
grasp on the subtler
muscle movements
required to make a truly
graceful face! It must be
hard being so
disconnected from...

Why are you staring at me
like my logic circuits have
malfunctioned, Captain? I
thought we were allies!
How could you even think
of siding with her!?
Very sorry. Very sorry. A\nscrew must have come\nloose or something.

It sounds like as good a
time as ever to sortie! Go
out there and bring those
bandits to justice!
No more signs of\nantagonistic life-forms.
False negative! It seems\none more remains!
Who are you and why do\nyou take umbrage with\n<font color=yellow>The Purge</font>?
The Purge? No such\nentry exists in my\ndatabase.

How dare you play the
victim! It is your
organization that defiles
planet after planet!

You will pay for the myriad
crimes you've committed,
though we may show you
some mercy if you come
quietly!
Hah. Can the treant's spell\nrestrain a mighty dragon?\nI think not.

Transporter activation
detected! He plans to flee
to a mothership orbiting
the planet!
A transporter? How could\nthis be?
It was so nice meeting you\nfor the first―and\nlast―time.
Unbelievable... We\nwere...ever so close...

So he has the ability to
flee at a moment's notice.
He probably only stayed
as long as he did to verify
our motives.

This is all my fault. I
should have scanned for
the appropriate signals as
soon as the enemy
appeared.

I am afraid that, with all
the malfunctioning parts
on this ship, pursuit is
impossible.

Even if it were, however,
we do not have sufficient
weaponry to engage them
in battle.
To have come all this way,\nonly to leave\nempty-handed...
Hey, we did save a planet.
We'll definitely get him\nnext time!
Let's eat our sorrows\naway!

My sentiments exactly! To
a T! We should be proud
of what we have
accomplished.
Still, he was right in front\nof us...
That we will! He is likely\nstill in this sector and\ncannot have gone far.
Moreover, clues as to his\nwhereabouts should\nabound!

I owe you a debt of
gratitude. It was
unbecoming of me to act
so weak, and thanks to
you, I can be myself again.
I fired up the replicator\nfor just such an occasion!\nTonight, we feast!

We have baby bananas,
Cavendish bananas,
manzano bananas, and
even plantains!
Henceforth, these fetes\nof fruit shall be known as\n'Bananapaloozas'!
You will have to forgive\nme if I never use that\nterm. Ever.

At any rate, we shan't find
that one-eyed tyrant if we
continue to lounge about
here. To the ship!
Orbital trajectory attained.
At least now we can put a\nname and a face to the\nillicit mining operation.
That, and utilize mid-range\ntransmissions once more.
We can!? Exquisite!

We can indeed, thanks to
the numerous spoils you
brought back from your
many battles.
Our communications can\nnow reach the length of\nthe average star system.
All the more serendipitous\nthat we uncovered the\norganization's name!

Thank you for reminding
me. I shall now take the
liberty to search for all
instances of "The Perv"
that I―

The Purge! P-U-R-G-E!
What sort of lascivious
materials have you been
reading of late!?
Oh, is that the name? I\nbeg your pardon.

How could anyone
program a dictionary
function so poorly!? I
swear, you behave more
like a human than a
machine.

Oh, would you look at that!
I have just finished
plotting a course to our
next star system. What
timing!

Even the way in which you
change the topic of
conversation reeks of
humanity.

If I didn't know any better,
I would say you are but an
actor adorned with a
robotic suit.
Aha. How about I put my\nhypothesis to the test and\nopen you up?

Captain, The Purge will not
wait for us! I suggest we
make for the next star
system...immediately!
To Be Continued in Future\nUpdates
